newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAP insider probe shows no wrongdoing, prosecutor says.
newsitem.headline: SAP insider probe shows no wrongdoing, prosecutor says.

text.p: State prosecutors said Thursday that an insider trading probe at software group SAP AG had produced no evidence of wrongdoing among 71 staff with direct access to corporate financial data.

Investigations would now concentrate on four employees with less access to sensitive information but surrounding whom there was still "a certain suspicion" of insider trading, a spokesman for the prosecutors' office said.
He added that none of the four employees was a member of SAP's management or supervisory boards and that the case could be closed in the coming weeks.
Earlier, SAP had said in a statement that, after questioning of company workers, the suspicion of illegal trading by so-called primary insiders had been "largely refuted."

Prosecutors had investigated whether some 100 SAP staff had dealt in stocks and derivatives to try to cash in ahead of poor quarterly results announced last October, which led to a fall of nearly a quarter in the company's share price.
